key_insight: RACER improves human-AI routing by estimating competence in a way that stays aligned with the expert’s role rather than relying on brittle class-specific shortcuts. It aims to preserve query-dependent decisions while avoiding spurious dependence on absolute class coordinates.
problem_solved: The paper addresses population-adaptive learning to defer: deciding when a model should act alone and when it should defer to an unseen human expert, using only a small context set of that expert’s past behavior. Existing methods can overfit to shortcuts or produce estimates that are too coarse within a class.
method: Introduces role-aligned competence estimation to model expert ability in a way that is tied to the decision role, not fixed class identity.
Builds on population-adaptive deferral settings where a context encoder uses a small set of expert examples to predict routing decisions for unseen experts.
Aims to avoid routing shortcuts seen in prior neural context encoders by replacing absolute class-coordinate dependence with role-indexed competence profiles.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this can make deferral systems more reliable and transferable across experts they have never seen before. It is especially relevant for safety-critical or high-stakes settings where routing mistakes can harm performance or trust.

paper_title: RACER: Role-Aligned Competence Estimation for Human-AI Routing
paper_authors: Joshua Strong, Emma Sun, Alexander Capstick, Pramit Saha, Cheng Ouyang
